title: EEOC reminds employers pre-employment health questionnaires may violate GINA
summary: The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission alleged that Dana Sealing Manufacturing illegally acquired genetic information.

title: This week in 5 numbers: Not even 5% of companies report ‘transformational’ outcomes from AI
summary: Here’s a roundup of numbers from the last week — including how many workers said their companies are trimming headcount.

title: Early career workers’ wages can’t match inflation, Glassdoor finds
summary: Greater purchasing power was thwarted by “higher energy prices due to the U.S.-Iran war,” research showed.

title: US health spending spikes to $5.7T in 2025, though growth should moderate, CMS finds
summary: Utilization — not cost growth — continues to accelerate spending, government actuaries said. Spiking prescription drug spending, including on GLP-1s, is especially acute.

title: What it takes to lead a dispersed front-line workforce
summary: For organizations with many hourly, distributed employees, workers must feel seen, heard and empowered to act with confidence, writes the CHRO of Fidium.

title: Broken recruiting processes block AI gains, survey shows
summary: Fragmented systems, isolated tools and siloed data are partly to blame, research from ManpowerGroup Talent Solutions and Everest Group said.

title: FCC Chairman says there is ‘common ground’ on ending illegal discrimination, DEI
summary: In May, 18 members of Congress sent a letter questioning the agency’s targeting of companies’ DEI policies.

title: AI may miss hidden talent. Recruiters can take steps to prevent that from happening.
summary: Employers must design AI systems that recognize nontraditional job candidates’ experience and credentials, a SHRM26 speaker said.

title: DEI’s next era? Reorientation, says SHRM’s Johnny Taylor Jr.
summary: In conversation with HR Dive, SHRM’s president and CEO forecasted the future of DEI in 2027 and 2028.

title: Younger workers may be falling behind in critical thinking skills
summary: The three largest skill gaps in the younger workforce represent “the very skills most essential to humans in the AI era,” per a report from Cangrade.
